experiments.title: MariaDB Introduction and Installation
theory_points: MariaDB is an open-source relational database management system (RDBMS), a fork of MySQL
It uses Structured Query Language (SQL) for managing and manipulating data
MariaDB supports ACID properties: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
Key features include high availability, scalability, and security
It stores data in tables with rows and columns, organized into databases
MariaDB runs as a server process and clients connect to it using TCP/IP or socket connections
applications: Web application backends
Data warehousing
E-commerce platforms
Content management systems

experiments.title: DDL Commands
theory_points: DDL (Data Definition Language) commands define and modify the structure of database objects
CREATE is used to create databases, tables, views, indexes, and other objects
ALTER modifies the structure of an existing table — add, drop, modify columns
DROP permanently removes a database object and its data
TRUNCATE removes all rows from a table but retains the table structure
RENAME changes the name of an existing database object
applications: Schema design and modification
Database migration scripts
Table restructuring during development

experiments.title: Constraints in SQL
theory_points: Constraints are rules enforced on data columns to ensure data integrity and accuracy
PRIMARY KEY uniquely identifies each record in a table — cannot be NULL or duplicate
FOREIGN KEY establishes a link between data in two tables, enforcing referential integrity
UNIQUE ensures all values in a column are distinct
NOT NULL prevents NULL values from being inserted into a column
CHECK validates that values in a column satisfy a specific condition
DEFAULT assigns a default value to a column when no value is specified during insertion
applications: Ensuring data integrity in relational databases
Maintaining referential integrity between related tables
Enforcing business rules at the database level
viva_topics: ON DELETE CASCADE vs SET NULL

experiments.title: DML Commands
theory_points: DML (Data Manipulation Language) commands are used to manipulate data within database tables
INSERT adds new rows of data into a table
UPDATE modifies existing data in one or more rows based on a condition
DELETE removes specific rows from a table based on a WHERE condition
SELECT retrieves data from one or more tables — the most frequently used SQL command
DML commands are not auto-committed and can be rolled back using ROLLBACK
applications: Data entry and modification in applications
Batch data updates and migrations
Data retrieval for reports and analytics
advantages: Can be conditional using WHERE clause

experiments.title: Built-in Functions and Clauses
theory_points: Aggregate functions perform calculations on a set of values and return a single result
COUNT() returns the number of rows, SUM() returns total, AVG() returns average
MAX() and MIN() return the highest and lowest values respectively
GROUP BY groups rows sharing common values into summary rows
HAVING filters groups created by GROUP BY — similar to WHERE but for aggregates
ORDER BY sorts the result set in ascending (ASC) or descending (DESC) order
String functions include UPPER(), LOWER(), LENGTH(), CONCAT(), SUBSTRING()
applications: Generating summary reports and analytics
Data aggregation for dashboards
Sorting and filtering large datasets
advantages: Efficient data summarization at database level

experiments.title: Joins in SQL
theory_points: Joins combine rows from two or more tables based on a related column between them
INNER JOIN returns only rows that have matching values in both tables
LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table
RIGHT JOIN returns all rows from the right table and matched rows from the left table
FULL OUTER JOIN returns all rows when there is a match in either table
CROSS JOIN produces the Cartesian product of both tables
SELF JOIN joins a table with itself, useful for hierarchical data
applications: Combining related data from multiple tables
Generating reports spanning multiple entities
Hierarchical data queries using self joins
advantages: Avoids data redundancy by normalizing into multiple tables

experiments.title: Subqueries in SQL
theory_points: A subquery is a query nested inside another SQL query (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE)
Single-row subqueries return one row and use operators like =, <, >, <=, >=
Multi-row subqueries return multiple rows and use IN, ANY, ALL operators
Correlated subqueries reference columns from the outer query and execute once per row
Scalar subqueries return a single value and can be used in SELECT or WHERE clauses
Subqueries can appear in WHERE, FROM (derived tables), SELECT, and HAVING clauses
applications: Complex filtering based on aggregated data
Dynamic value comparisons across tables
Creating derived tables for complex analysis
advantages: Break complex queries into manageable parts
Can replace multiple JOINs in some scenarios
Support dynamic value computation within queries

experiments.title: Set Operations in SQL
theory_points: Set operations combine results of two or more SELECT statements
UNION combines results and removes duplicate rows from the output
UNION ALL combines results and retains all rows including duplicates
INTERSECT returns only rows that appear in both result sets
EXCEPT (or MINUS) returns rows from the first query that do not appear in the second
All set operations require the SELECT statements to have the same number and compatible data types of columns
applications: Combining data from similar tables or partitions
Finding common records across datasets
Identifying differences between two data sets

experiments.title: Views in SQL
theory_points: A view is a virtual table based on the result of a SELECT query
Views do not store data physically — they reference underlying base tables
CREATE VIEW defines a view, and DROP VIEW removes it
Updatable views allow INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE if they meet specific conditions
WITH CHECK OPTION ensures that modifications through the view satisfy the view's WHERE condition
Views provide data abstraction, security, and simplify complex queries
applications: Data security by restricting access to specific columns/rows
Simplifying complex multi-table queries for end users
Creating logical data abstractions
advantages: Enhance security by limiting data exposure

experiments.title: Control Structures in SQL
theory_points: Control structures in SQL allow conditional execution and iteration within stored programs
IF-THEN-ELSE executes different blocks of code based on a Boolean condition
CASE expression provides multi-way conditional logic — similar to switch-case
LOOP creates an unconditional loop that repeats until a LEAVE statement is encountered
WHILE loop repeats a block of code as long as a specified condition remains true
REPEAT loop executes at least once, then repeats until a condition becomes true
ITERATE skips the remaining code in a loop and starts the next iteration
LEAVE exits a loop or block immediately
applications: Implementing business logic in stored procedures
Iterative data processing within the database
Conditional data transformations
advantages: Reduce round-trips between application and database
Enable complex logic execution at database level

experiments.title: Exception Handling in SQL
theory_points: Exception handling in SQL manages runtime errors within stored programs (procedures, functions, triggers)
DECLARE HANDLER defines a handler that executes when a specific condition occurs
Handler types: CONTINUE (resumes execution), EXIT (terminates the block), UNDO (rolls back)
SQLEXCEPTION handles all SQL error conditions
SQLWARNING handles warning conditions and NOT FOUND handles empty cursors
SIGNAL raises a user-defined exception with a custom error message
RESIGNAL re-raises a caught exception, optionally modifying its attributes
applications: Graceful error recovery in stored procedures
Custom error messages for application-level handling
Transaction safety with proper rollback on errors
advantages: Prevents stored program crashes on errors
Enables custom error codes and messages

experiments.title: Functions and Procedures in SQL
theory_points: A stored procedure is a precompiled set of SQL statements stored in the database for reuse
A stored function returns a single value and can be used within SQL expressions
Procedures use IN (input), OUT (output), and INOUT (both) parameters
Functions must have a RETURNS clause specifying the return data type
DELIMITER changes the statement delimiter to allow semicolons inside procedure/function body
Procedures are called using CALL, while functions are invoked within SELECT or expressions
Both improve performance through precompilation and reduce network traffic
applications: Encapsulating business logic at the database level
Reusable code modules for common database operations
Batch data processing and complex calculations
advantages: Reduce code duplication and network traffic
Provide abstraction and security through encapsulation

experiments.title: Triggers in SQL
theory_points: A trigger is a stored program that automatically executes in response to DML events on a table
BEFORE triggers execute before the triggering DML operation is performed
AFTER triggers execute after the triggering DML operation is completed
Triggers can be defined for INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE events
NEW refers to the new row data (available in INSERT and UPDATE triggers)
OLD refers to the existing row data (available in UPDATE and DELETE triggers)
Triggers are used for auditing, validation, enforcing complex business rules, and maintaining derived data
applications: Audit logging — tracking data changes automatically
Data validation beyond CHECK constraints
Maintaining denormalized summary tables
Enforcing complex cross-table business rules
advantages: Automatic execution — no explicit call needed
